data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between idempotent and safe is best understood through counterexample. A writer that appends a random UUID per call is safe (retries don't corrupt the log) but not idempotent (each retry produces a different entry). A writer that appends a deterministic hash of the payload is both safe and idempotent (same payload always yields the same entry, deduplicatable). A writer that increments a global counter and appends the result is neither safe nor idempotent (retries corrupt the counter and produce divergent entries). The append-only log requires the safe-and-non-idempotent writer at minimum, but prefers the safe-and-idempotent writer for robust deterministic replay.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If payload content is genuinely unique per logical event (e.g., two distinct payments of the same amount), then a deterministic hash writer would incorrectly collapse them\u2014a case where idempotency keys must be separate from content hashes","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the replay processor has no access to content (encrypted log), then only idempotency keys work, and safe-but-non-idempotent writers require the keys to be present","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If external mutable state (like the counter) is also logged as an event, then even (c) can be made replay-safe by treating the counter as a derived projection rather than an independent store","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Three archetypes: (a) random UUID writer\u2014safe, non-idempotent; the log has duplicates but replay can filter by content hash if payloads are identical. (b) deterministic hash writer\u2014safe and idempotent; the log or processor can collapse exact-duplicate entries. (c) counter-incrementing writer\u2014neither safe nor idempotent; retries corrupt the counter state and produce semantically distinct entries that replay cannot distinguish from genuine new events. The log's minimum requirement is (a): safe writers that don't corrupt external state on retry. The log's ideal requirement is (b): idempotent writers whose duplicates are trivially detectable. The log absolutely cannot tolerate (c).","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
